title: p-adic Algebraic Closure: [ℚ̄_p : ℚ_p] = ∞
description: Proves the p-adic contrast to the real case: while [ℂ:ℝ] = 2 (parent entry), the algebraic closure of ℚ_p has infinite degree over ℚ_p. The key vehicle is the polynomial X^n - p, which is irreducible over ℚ_p for every n ≥ 1 (Newton polygon argument, axiomatized), so ℚ_p has field extensions of all degrees. The degree-n statement is machine-checked: AdjoinRoot(X^n - p) has ℚ_p-dimension exactly n.

(2) padic_alg_closure_infinite_dim — the algebraic closure of ℚ_p is not finite-dimensional over ℚ_p (follows from unbounded extension degrees, but connecting to Module.Finite on AlgebraicClosure requires additional infrastructure).

overview.historicalContext:
The real numbers are exceptional among fields: they need only one quadratic extension (ℂ = ℝ(i)) to become algebraically closed. Hensel's p-adic numbers (1897), the completions of ℚ at prime p, behave very differently. The algebraic closure ℚ̄_p requires extensions of all degrees.

This follows from Hensel's lemma (1897): if f ∈ ℤ_p[X] and f has a simple root modulo p, then it has a root in ℤ_p. But X^n - p has no root modulo p (its Newton polygon has slope -1/n ≠ 0), so X^n - p is irreducible over ℚ_p — giving extensions of degree n for all n.

The contrast between [ℂ:ℝ] = 2 and [ℚ̄_p:ℚ_p] = ∞ is a fundamental distinction between real and p-adic completions of ℚ. It is captured algebraically by the Artin-Schreier theorem: ℝ is real-closed (one quadratic extension suffices), while ℚ_p is not real-closed (it needs infinitely many extensions).
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (OQ-04 from FundamentalTheoremAlgebraOQ04)**: Formalize the p-adic contrast — [ℚ̄_p : ℚ_p] = ∞ and the completion ℂ_p is algebraically closed by Krasner's lemma — showing that 'one extension suffices' is special to real-closed fields.

**Partial answer here**: [ℚ_p(p^{1/n}) : ℚ_p] = n for all n (machine-checked), so ℚ_p has extensions of every degree. The conclusion [ℚ̄_p : ℚ_p] = ∞ is axiomatized (non-finiteness follows directly but requires AlgebraicClosure infrastructure).
overview.text: Formalization contrasting the algebraic closures of ℝ and ℚ_p. While the parent proves [ℂ:ℝ] = 2, this entry proves ℚ_p has field extensions of every degree n (AdjoinRoot(X^n - p) has dimension n, machine-checked), then axiomatizes the corollary [ℚ̄_p:ℚ_p] = ∞. The p-adic irreducibility X^n - p over ℚ_p is also axiomatized (Newton polygon argument — see mathematical sketch in the Lean file).
overview.proofStrategy:
Two independent components:

**1. Degree-n extensions (proved)**: The polynomial f = X^n - p has natDegree n over ℚ_p. The `AdjoinRoot.powerBasis` construction gives a ℚ_p-basis of AdjoinRoot(f) of size natDegree(f) = n. Combined with the axiom that f is irreducible (giving AdjoinRoot(f) a field structure), this yields [AdjoinRoot(f):ℚ_p] = n.

**2. Irreducibility over ℚ_p (axiom)**: X^n - p satisfies the Eisenstein criterion over ℤ_p at the maximal ideal (p). Since ℤ_p is a DVR, Gauss's lemma applies: irreducibility over ℤ_p implies irreducibility over ℚ_p = Frac(ℤ_p). The Newton polygon formulation: single segment from (0,1) to (n,0) with slope -1/n, gcd(1,n)=1 implies irreducibility. Both arguments are mathematically sound but require bridging PadicInt to Mathlib's DVR infrastructure.
keyInsights: **Exceptional position of ℝ**: The Artin-Schreier theorem characterizes real-closed fields as exactly those whose algebraic closure is a degree-2 extension. ℝ is the prototypical real-closed field; ℚ_p is not real-closed (it lacks a square root of -1 for p ≡ 3 mod 4, and even when it doesn't, extensions of all degrees exist via ramified extensions).

**Newton polygon argument**: For X^n - p over ℚ_p, the Newton polygon has a single segment with slope -1/n. When gcd(1,n) = 1 (always true), a single-slope Newton polygon implies the polynomial is irreducible — this is a fundamental result in p-adic analysis.

**AdjoinRoot finrank**: The key machine-checked result is Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (AdjoinRoot(X^n - C p)) = n, proved using the PowerBasis construction. This is a general algebraic fact about adjoin-root algebras that doesn't require the irreducibility axiom — just that the polynomial is nonzero.

**Two axioms, different strengths**: Xn_sub_p_irred_Qp (irreducibility) implies padic_alg_closure_infinite_dim (infinite dimension) but not conversely. We axiomatize both because the second requires AlgebraicClosure infrastructure beyond what's proved.
prerequisites: Field extensions and vector space dimension ([K:F] = dim_F K)
p-adic numbers ℚ_p and p-adic integers ℤ_p (DVR structure)
Eisenstein criterion and Gauss's lemma for polynomials

sections.title: Part I: Real Case — [ℂ:ℝ] = 2 (Reference)
sections.summary: References the parent result: [ℂ:ℝ] = 2 and ℂ is the unique algebraic closure of ℝ.
sections.mathContext: $[\mathbb{C}:\mathbb{R}] = 2$ via Mathlib's `Complex.finrank_real_complex`. Starting point for the contrast.

sections.title: Part II: X^n - p Irreducible over ℚ
sections.summary: Proves X^n - p irreducible over ℤ (Eisenstein at prime ideal (p)) and over ℚ (Gauss's lemma via NthRootIrrationalOQ01).
sections.mathContext: Eisenstein criterion at $(p) \subset \mathbb{Z}$: leading coeff $= 1 \not\in (p)$, all non-leading coefficients $\in (p)$, constant term $-p \in (p) \setminus (p^2)$. Gauss: primitive + irreducible over $\mathbb{Z}$ implies irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$.

sections.title: Part III: Newton Polygon Axiom
sections.summary: Axiom: X^n - p is irreducible over ℚ_p (Newton polygon, single segment slope -1/n).
sections.mathContext: Newton polygon of $X^n - p$ at $p$: single segment from $(0, v_p(p)) = (0,1)$ to $(n, 0)$ with slope $-1/n$. Since $\gcd(1,n)=1$, the Ore-Hensel theorem gives irreducibility.

sections.title: Part IV: Degree-n Extensions of ℚ_p
sections.summary: Proves natDegree(X^n - C p over ℚ_p) = n and Module.finrank ℚ_[p] (AdjoinRoot(X^n - p)) = n via AdjoinRoot.powerBasis.
sections.mathContext: $[\mathbb{Q}_p(p^{1/n}):\mathbb{Q}_p] = n$: the power basis of $\mathrm{AdjoinRoot}(X^n-p)$ has size $= \mathrm{natDegree}(X^n-p) = n$.

sections.title: Part V: [ℚ̄_p : ℚ_p] = ∞
sections.summary: Axiom: AlgebraicClosure(ℚ_p) is not finite-dimensional over ℚ_p. Proved contrast theorem.
sections.mathContext: Unbounded extensions (degree $n$ for all $n$) imply $[\overline{\mathbb{Q}_p}:\mathbb{Q}_p] = \infty$. The Lean formulation uses $\neg\,\mathrm{Module.Finite}$.

sections.title: Part VI: Contrast and Summary
sections.summary: Contrast theorem (finrank ℝ ℂ = 2 AND ¬Module.Finite ℚ_[p] (AlgClosure ℚ_[p])), explicit examples n=2,3,4, and summary conjunction.
sections.mathContext: The real/p-adic dichotomy in one theorem: real algebraic closure is degree 2; p-adic algebraic closure is infinite-dimensional.

openQuestions: Can the Newton polygon argument (Xn_sub_p_irred_Qp axiom) be formally proved using Mathlib's PadicInt as a DVR and the DVR Gauss lemma?
Formalize Krasner's lemma: if α is separable algebraic over ℚ_p and |α - β|_p is small enough, then ℚ_p(α) = ℚ_p(β) — giving the completion ℂ_p = (ℚ̄_p)^∧ is algebraically closed
Compare with the function-field case: for F_q((t)), the algebraic closure also has infinite degree, and the Puiseux series give extensions X^n - t
